Tide Tables Explained

A tide table lists the predicted times and heights of high and low water for a place. Read the full guide before sailing, because the numbers differ by harbour and by season, and a wrong guess can ground a boat.

Reading the table

Each row gives a day. Heights are in metres above chart datum and times are local. The pattern repeats roughly every twelve hours and twenty-five minutes, which is why the times shift later each day.

A note on code

Harbour offices publish the same numbers as data. A small helper can convert them, for example:

const h = rows.map(r => r.height);\nconsole.log(Math.max(...h));

Always cross-check against the local notice to mariners before you rely on any computed value for passage planning.
